predictions: P-A (BB union rule): the new 4-detector fits will pass the union rule (LRT_BANDBB_BAND>=9.2 & kT>1.05 OR LRT_CPLBB_CPL>=9.2 & kT>1.05) in the TIME-INTEGRATED spectrum and in >=7 resolved blocks, AND the preferred Band+BB kT population will STAY LOW - median kT in 2-6 keV, no block above 20 keV except possibly the last. Archival (7-det): union in 10/11 resolved blocks + integrated; Band+BB kT median 3.24 keV, range 1.93-6.21 keV; integrated LRT_BANDBB_BAND = 140.19, LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 92.10. FALSIFIED IF the union count collapses to <=3 resolved blocks, OR the median Band+BB kT comes out >20 keV. *** THIS IS THE SHARPEST DIFF IN THE WHOLE BURST: the literature's thermal component sits at TENS of keV - McGlynn 2012 measures kT = 61.3 (+0.7/-0.6) keV integrated over 0-52.7 s and kT decaying ~100 -> ~40 keV across ~25 bins; Iyyani+2015's Band+BB kT also falls smoothly over the pulse. Our archival kT ~ 3 keV is ~20x lower. Either (a) our BB is the L28 edge-constrained low-kT class pinned at the 8.1 keV NaI floor and is a DIFFERENT feature from the literature's thermal peak, or (b) our BB multistart is landing in a low-kT local minimum (the known BB seed-poisoning failure mode). Both are testable: if the new fits reproduce kT ~ 3 keV with the SAME detector set the literature used (n0,n1,n3,b0 - identical), then (b) is a live suspicion and the Band+BB start grid must be probed at kT = 40-100 keV explicitly. ***

P-A2 (two-break): LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 will persist in the TIME-INTEGRATED spectrum and in >=6 resolved blocks. Archival: integrated 70.07; >=9.2 in 9 of 10 testable resolved blocks (blk2 14.79, blk3 70.38, blk4 38.30, blk5 44.90, blk6 29.55, blk7 29.86, blk8 37.34, blk9 18.27, blk10 11.53; only blk1 = 5.10 fails, blk0 untestable). This makes bn110920546 one of the STRONGEST two-break bursts in the archival census. FALSIFIED IF integrated LRT_DSBPL_SBPL < 9.2. Independent literature corroboration, from a completely different model family: Iyyani+2015's best model is 2 blackbodies + power law, i.e. an explicitly TWO-BREAK spectrum, with the low break E_i = 200 -> 8 keV (break at 12.9 +/- 1.7 s) and the high break E_C = ~500 -> 40 keV (break at 13.2 +/- 2.4 s); Sharma V.+2020 restates it as 'multiple spectral breaks'. PREDICTION P-A2b: the DSBPL break RATIO xp/xb will DECREASE with time, tracking Iyyani's E_C/E_i which is <=3 and declining. Archival ratios: integrated 255.19/37.07 = 6.9; blk7 180.68/10.08 = 17.9; blk8 145.93/10.00 = 14.6; blk9 120.58/79.99 = 1.5; blk10 103.93/24.36 = 4.3 - NOISY, several xb values railed at the 10 keV floor or at ~900 keV, so this sub-prediction is weak and is flagged as such in advance.

P-A3 (BB vs DSBPL are RIVALS, not two components): per L25 (xb ~ 3.92*kT, r=0.87), an archival kT ~ 3.2 keV implies xb ~ 12.6 keV, and the archival DSBPL xb rails at 10.0-10.1 keV in exactly the blocks (7,8) where Band+BB is the AIC winner. PREDICT an L12-style degeneracy: the low DSBPL break and the low-kT BB describe the SAME low-energy feature. FALSIFIED IF the new fits give a well-constrained xb far from ~4*kT in the majority of union blocks.

P-B (literature frame, integrated - WITH A COVERAGE CAVEAT THAT DOMINATES): our new time-integrated Band fit over the stamped window -3.240 -> +111.304 s will give Ep = 220-290 keV, alpha = -0.30..+0.05, beta = -2.0..-2.5, all well-constrained. FALSIFIED IF integrated Ep < 150 keV or > 400 keV, or if beta is unconstrained/railed. Frames to diff against, each with its component coverage (T9): (i) GBM catalog flnc_band over -3.584 -> +245.252 s, dets b0/n0/n1/n3: Ep = 247.81 (+4.24/-4.06) keV, alpha = -0.537 +/- 0.015, beta = -3.133 (+0.268/-0.193), chi2r = 1.1187/481 - FULL pulse plus 80 s of tail; (ii) McGlynn 2012 over +0.003 -> +52.737 s, same detectors: Ep = 334 +/- 5 keV, alpha = -0.20 +/- 0.02, beta = -2.65 (+0.07/-0.09), C-stat 3206.5/485 - FIRST THIRD of the pulse; (iii) archival 7-det run over -2.103 -> +120.240 s: Ep = 254.75, alpha = -0.111, beta = -2.168. *** COVERAGE PREDICTION: because our window stops at 111.3 s and T90 runs 5.12 -> 165.89 s, we omit the softest ~55 s of the pulse; our integrated alpha must therefore come out HARDER than the catalog's -0.537 and our beta HARDER (less negative) than the catalog's -3.13. If instead we reproduce alpha = -0.54 on a window that excludes the soft tail, something is wrong with our background or response, not with the catalog. ***

P-B2 (evolution class - MONOTONIC HARD-TO-SOFT, and this one is unanimous): block-resolved Band Ep will DECAY MONOTONICALLY across the window with NO mid-burst rise and NO intensity tracking, falling from ~250-500 keV in the first blocks to ~100-140 keV in the last. Every era agrees: Yu+2016 'GRB 100707032, GRB 110721200, and GRB 110920546 are single pulsed, FRED bursts. All of them show pure hard-to-soft behaviour'; Yu+2019 Table 1 class 'h.t.s.'; Wang+2024 RAA class 'h.t.s.'; Iyyani+2015 Ep 700 -> 50 keV as a broken power law with break at 28 +/- 3 s (indices -0.35 +/- 0.07 then -0.95 +/- 0.02); Yu+2016's own table falls 492 -> 150 keV over bins 1-17; archival falls 585 -> 109 keV over blocks 2-10. FALSIFIED IF Ep peaks in a middle block (intensity tracking) or rises anywhere by more than its errors. SUB-PREDICTION P-B2b: the Ep(t) decay will be BROKEN, not a single power law, with the break near 12-30 s - Iyyani places it at 28 +/- 3 s for Band-only and at 12.9-13.2 s for the 2BB peaks; Tak+2023 independently finds the only clear Ep-F_nu,Ep break in their sample for this burst (delta = 0.7 +/- 0.1 before, 2.1 +/- 1.0 after).

P-B3 (the LINE OF DEATH - the burst's defining feature): the new block-resolved Band alpha will exceed the slow-cooling synchrotron limit alpha = -2/3 in EVERY block, and will exceed alpha = 0 in at least 3 late blocks. Literature: Iyyani+2015 'alpha is found to lie above -0.4 through out the burst, which is inconsistent with both slow cooling (alpha <= -0.67) and fast cooling (alpha <= -1.5)' and 'after 70 s, alpha lies above 0 ... among the hardest GRB spectra ever observed'; Ryde+2019 alpha_b = +0.23 (+0.11/-0.13); Lu+2018 tabulates alpha = +0.10, +0.08, +0.02 over 0-15 s; Yu+2016 bin 17 (58.9-67.1 s) alpha = +0.025 +/- 0.080; archival alpha runs -0.11 (integrated) and crosses zero at block 5 (t ~ 24 s), reaching +0.33 by block 9. FALSIFIED IF any block returns a well-constrained alpha < -0.67. NOTE THE OPEN INCONSISTENCY WE MUST NOT SILENTLY RESOLVE (T5/L26): our archival alpha crosses zero at ~24 s, Iyyani says ~70 s, and Wang+2024 RAA classifies the alpha evolution as 'FLAT' while Iyyani says it rises linearly from -0.4 to +0.8. Also Lu+2018 (alpha ~ +0.1) and Yu+2016 (alpha ~ -0.4) disagree on the SAME early intervals.

P-B4 (high-energy index / BGO dropout): beta will DEGRADE after ~60 s and the last blocks will prefer a curved-but-unbroken or power-law-like shape. Iyyani+2015 verbatim: 'After 60 s there was no significant BGO emission'; Yu+2016's catalog best models go COMP -> PL at 67 s and 'none' (unfittable) after 102.9 s - i.e. the published record says the data stop constraining a peak inside our window. Archival: blocks 9 and 10 (70.9-120.2 s) switch AIC winner to SBPLfree, and beta steepens to -3.08 / -3.52. PREDICT the same handover. FALSIFIED IF beta stays well-constrained near -2.3 in the last block.

P-C (identity and data provenance - NOT a fit target): ZERO GCN circulars (verified by two endpoints with a positive control). NO redshift, NO afterglow (Iyyani+2015 verbatim). NO LAT and NO LLE detection (Iyyani+2015 verbatim; no gll_* files locally or in the FSSC current/ directory; grb_sample HAS_LAT = False). GBM-only, four detectors n0/n1/n3/b0 at 26.96 / 48.41 / 28.85 / 79.09 deg - IDENTICAL to the set used by the GBM catalogue, McGlynn 2012 and Iyyani+2015, so a detector-set explanation for any disagreement is CLOSED IN ADVANCE. The P3 diff frame = GBM catalog scat v01 (flnc + pflx, 4 models) + Yu+2016's 22-row published block table + the Iyyani/McGlynn/Shenoy/Burgess dedicated chain.

P-D (data-quality prediction, falsifiable at the background stage): the pre-burst background is contaminated by SAA activation decay. Fermi exited the SAA at t - T0 = -120.1 s (verified locally from data/bn110920546/glg_poshist_all_110920_v01.fit FLAGS bit1 transitioning 1 -> 0, NOT merely quoted), and Biltzinger+2020 §4.1 uses THIS BURST as their showcase that 'the classical approach of using polynomial fits can give ambiguous answers' here. Our stamped pre-burst windows (n0 [-16.54,-5.54], n1/n3 [-19.53,-9.00], b0 [-16.54,-6.54] s) lie entirely inside that decaying tail. PREDICT: the pre-burst polynomial residuals will show systematic curvature, and the fitted background level in the first block will be the largest single systematic on the low-energy shoulder (i.e. on exactly the low-kT BB / low DSBPL break that P-A and P-A3 are about). FALSIFIED IF the pre-burst residuals are flat and structureless.
